title: AAU Entrepreneurship Masters-equivalent Program
design_goal: Top-university graduate-level demonstrated competence, not credential imitation.
benchmark_basis: HBS broad required management core plus Entrepreneurial Manager
Wharton cross-functional MBA core plus Entrepreneurship & Innovation
Stanford analytical/leadership/management foundations plus experiential entrepreneurship and Startup Garage

evidence_rules: Use current external research when material claims depend on current facts.
Preserve source provenance when research is used.
Narrative claims alone do not count as mastery.

courses.title: Financial Accounting and Reporting
courses.description: Interpret and construct decision-useful financial statements for ventures.
units: Construct linked income statement, balance sheet and cash-flow logic for a new venture.
Build a three-statement mini-model for a hypothetical venture and explain every linkage.
Reason about recognition, gross margin, inventory/receivables/payables and cash conversion.
Analyze a case where reported profit rises while cash deteriorates; identify causes and fixes.
Use contribution margin, fixed/variable costs and cost allocation for decisions.
Compare two delivery models and recommend one using contribution margin and relevant-cost analysis.
Use financial statements to make an operating decision.
Write a CFO-style memo diagnosing venture health and specifying three actions with quantified effects.

courses.title: Corporate Finance and Capital Allocation
courses.description: Evaluate financing, investment, risk, and capital-allocation decisions.
objectives: Time value and discounted cash flow
units: Apply discounting, NPV and scenario valuation.
Value a staged investment under base/upside/downside cash-flow scenarios.
Relate uncertainty, risk premium and financing cost.
Explain how business risk changes hurdle rates and capital allocation.
Compare mutually exclusive investments under uncertainty.
Choose between two growth projects using NPV, sensitivity and strategic constraints.
Recommend a financing mix for a venture with explicit dilution, default and runway tradeoffs.

courses.title: Managerial Economics and Market Structure
courses.description: Use economic reasoning to make pricing, capacity, and market-entry decisions.
units: Estimate elasticity and connect it to revenue and pricing.
Given a demand schedule, estimate elasticity and identify the revenue-maximizing direction of price change.
Use marginal cost, marginal revenue and opportunity cost.
Solve a capacity-allocation case with scarce compute or labor.
Analyze monopoly, oligopoly and competitive dynamics.
Map a market structure and predict likely competitor responses to entry.
Integrate economics into entry and pricing.
Recommend whether and how to enter a market using demand, cost and competitive evidence.

courses.title: Marketing, Customer Discovery and Sales
courses.description: Find customers, test needs, position value, and build a repeatable sales process.
units: Design 12 non-leading discovery questions and a falsifiable interview plan.
Choose an ICP and differentiated position.
Segment a mixed market and defend a beachhead ICP and positioning statement.
Relate funnel conversion, CAC and payback.
Build a funnel model from impressions to revenue and calculate CAC and payback.
Design a repeatable B2B or B2C selling motion.
Create qualification, discovery, objection-handling and close criteria for a first sales process.

courses.title: Operations and Supply Chain
courses.description: Design reliable, scalable operations with measurable service and cost performance.
units: Map throughput, cycle time and constraints.
Diagnose a multi-step process and calculate the binding bottleneck and throughput.
Reason about utilization, waits and service levels.
Analyze a service system under demand spikes and propose capacity policy.
Design controls that reduce defects without waste.
Create a quality plan for a high-consequence service with measurable failure thresholds.
Design vendors, inventory/service redundancy and incident response.
Produce an operating plan that survives a supplier or infrastructure failure.

courses.title: Organizational Behavior and Leadership
courses.description: Build teams, incentives, decision systems, and leadership practices suited to growth.
units: Align incentives with desired behavior and avoid gaming.
Redesign a flawed compensation system that rewards volume but harms quality.
Structure roles, decision rights and conflict resolution.
Create a team operating model with RACI-like ownership and escalation rules.
Write a leadership response to a major strategic setback with decision rationale.
Define hiring bars, performance systems and cultural mechanisms.
Build a first-10-hires plan including scorecards, incentives and failure modes.

courses.title: Strategy and Competitive Analysis
courses.description: Create and defend advantage using industry, capability, and game-theoretic analysis.
units: Use industry-structure analysis without treating it mechanically.
Analyze attractiveness, power and profit pools in a chosen industry.
Assess whether a venture advantage is valuable, scarce, difficult to copy and organizationally supported.
Anticipate retaliation, entry and strategic moves.
Run a competitor-response scenario for a new entrant.
Design advantage using network effects, switching costs, data, brand or complements.
Produce a strategy memo specifying moat claims, evidence, vulnerabilities and tests.

courses.title: Business Law, Ethics and Governance
courses.description: Recognize legal, ethical, governance, and fiduciary constraints in venture decisions.
units: Understand entity, agency, liability and contract mechanics.
Review a hypothetical founder/service agreement and identify key legal-economic risks.
Recognize IP ownership, privacy/data and worker classification issues.
Identify legal-risk controls for a software venture handling customer data.
Understand boards, duties, conflicts and approval rights.
Resolve a board conflict involving financing and related-party interests.
Make principled decisions beyond minimum legal compliance.
Write a governance memo for a profitable action that is legal but creates material stakeholder harm.

courses.title: Data Analysis and Managerial Decision Making
courses.description: Use data, experiments, forecasts, and uncertainty to make defensible decisions.
units: Use distributions, segmentation and visualization conceptually.
Diagnose a KPI dataset and separate signal from aggregation artifacts.
Use expected value, Bayesian updating and decision trees.
Build a decision tree for launch vs delay with uncertain demand.
Design an A/B or quasi-experiment with metric, sample and stopping logic.
Build forecasts with explicit assumptions and stress tests.
Create a 12-month forecast with base/upside/downside assumptions and sensitivity ranking.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship Opportunity Identification
courses.description: Discover, frame, and prioritize opportunities worth pursuing.
units: Create a problem inventory with evidence, severity, frequency and existing workaround.
Estimate bottom-up TAM/SAM/SOM without market-report substitution.
Build a bottom-up market estimate from customer count, usage and realistic price.
Match opportunity to capabilities, resources and access.
Compare three opportunities against capability, capital, access and time constraints.
Use explicit kill criteria before attachment forms.
Rank four opportunities with falsifiable assumptions and precommitted kill criteria.

courses.title: Business Model Design and Validation
courses.description: Turn an opportunity into a falsifiable business model and validation plan.
units: Map jobs, pains, gains and switching behavior.
Create a value proposition tied to observed customer evidence rather than generic benefits.
Compare subscription, transaction, usage, services and hybrid models.
Model three revenue architectures and identify incentive and cash-flow differences.
Map key activities, partners and cost drivers.
Build an activity-based cost model for an MVP and scaled state.
Convert business model into ranked testable assumptions.
Produce an assumption map with cheapest decisive test for each critical uncertainty.

courses.title: Venture Finance, Bootstrapping and Fundraising
courses.description: Finance a venture through disciplined bootstrapping and external capital choices.
units: Calculate burn, runway, financing gap and milestone timing.
Build a financing-need schedule tied to operating milestones.
Use revenue, pre-sales, services and non-dilutive funding strategically.
Design a bootstrapped path and identify where it becomes strategically constraining.
Model ownership, dilution, debt service and investor returns.
Construct a cap-table scenario across two financing rounds.
Match capital source to stage, risk and bargaining power.
Write an investor strategy with target investor type, use of funds, milestones and walk-away terms.

courses.title: Pricing, Unit Economics and Cash Flow
courses.description: Build economically coherent pricing, contribution margin, CAC/LTV, and cash plans.
units: Choose value metric, package and willingness-to-pay test.
Design three pricing packages and a test that can disconfirm willingness-to-pay assumptions.
Calculate gross margin, contribution margin and break-even.
Build a unit economics model including variable compute/data/service costs.
Calculate acquisition, retention, LTV and payback without vanity metrics.
Evaluate two channels using cohort retention, CAC, LTV and payback.
Integrate price, volume, burn and runway.
Create a 12-month cash plan and specify triggers for hiring freeze, price change or shutdown.

courses.title: Go-to-Market, Product-Market Fit and Growth
courses.description: Design GTM systems, measure product-market fit, and scale without destroying economics.
units: Select an initial market and channel based on economics and access.
Choose a beachhead and channel mix with explicit rejection of weaker alternatives.
Design low-cost tests of demand and acquisition.
Create a four-week GTM experiment backlog with success/failure thresholds.
Distinguish traction from PMF using retention, pull and willingness-to-pay.
Evaluate a dataset and decide whether PMF evidence is sufficient, weak or absent.
Scale only when retention and economics support it.
Design a growth plan with capacity, CAC, retention and cash constraints.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Execution Capstone
courses.description: Integrate the full program by taking a venture from opportunity through an evidence-backed build/revise/kill decision.
units: Select one opportunity and state customer, problem, evidence and falsifiable thesis.
Submit the capstone venture thesis plus customer/problem evidence and kill criteria.
Integrate revenue, costs, pricing, capital and scenarios.
Submit business model, pricing, unit economics, 18-month cash model and financing plan.
Integrate launch plan, operating model, governance and risk.
Submit GTM, operating plan, risk register, legal/governance assumptions and stress tests.
Defend assumptions and choose build, revise or kill.
Present the integrated case, answer adversarial objections, and make an evidence-backed build/revise/kill decision.
